_help.about: Fire pots (Mike, 6 Oct, 22:32): a small sealed vessel of oil with a wick, lit off the torch in your right hand and thrown. Rare; you never craft them (§BN): restored ruins' folk give them (§FF.3). The only ranged way to fight back in Torchfire 1, and it is fire (§ED.7: only fire answers what lurks in the dark). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct night; the designer owns them. Wired 7 Oct (Claude Code, prompt 60; FirePots, ThrownPot, PotFire, PotMesh in scripts/crawler/): everything here is read, with the engine's own blocks added below (wick, look, found, dev_items, spread, hurts_you). sources: found (one pot in a side room per dungeon) and F9 are in; gift waits for §FF.3. What burns and what is driven off join through FirePots' fire-target socket: prompt 49's snake (driven off; it notices the wick and hears the burst) and prompt 58's skeletons (burnt down by fire_hp times oil_scale and gone at 0; a sleeping one wakes burning; awake, they see the wick and hear the burst) are in. The spine the found pot keeps off is the way from the hearth room to the heart until queue 46's is built.
_help.vessel: §FJ.5 (Mike, 6 Oct 22:52: 'the clay pot bomb sounds good'): a sealed fired-clay pot with a wick (answers §FA.5; fits §EH). No glass.
_help.sources: §FA.3 / §FF.3. gift: the folk of a fully relit ruin give some, with the way of using them (Mike). found: a few lie in ruins (Claude's first guess, open).
_help.carry_max: How many fit the left-hand strip (§FB). Rarity is the point: there won't be many (Mike).
_help.lit_from: §FA.3 (Mike): the wick is lit off the lit torch in the right hand only. No lit torch, no pot (§AW: fire is borrowed, never made). light_anim_s: the hands-come-together animation, in view.
_help.fuse_s: Seconds from the wick catching to the burst (Claude's first guess). cook_off_in_hand: null until Mike answers §FI.2 call 2; true would make a pot held past fuse_s burst in your hand as one hit (harm.json). Mike answered 7 Oct ("a fuse held too long after lighting will explode in hand and cause 1 point of damage"): true, wired (Claude Code, FirePots._cook_off): held past fuse_s from the catch, the pot bursts where your hand is (its whole burst: the flash, the fire on what stands within splash_m, tar's patch, the sound), it is gone from your pack, and you take one hit of harm.json's three (death cause fire:pot_in_hand). false or null: a spent fuse waits for the impact, as first built.
_help.throw: §FB first guess: hold left click to light and aim (the §N hold-to-charge), release to lob. Range grows with the hold from min_m to max_m over charge_s.
_help.gives_away: §FA.3 first guess (§DF): the wick's flare is seen by creatures within flare_seen_m with a line of sight; the burst is heard within burst_heard_m. Wired 7 Oct on the snake (queue 60 part 2): the wick's flare counts as your flame in its sight out to flare_seen_m, even with your torch smothered; a burst within burst_heard_m of it counts as a sprint heard.
_help.spreads_to: §FA.3 first guess: what catches from a burst or a burning patch (webs, the temple cats' wooden runs, dry rushes, cloth).
_help.light: Its fire lights in the hearth's amber (§EX.6, look.json fire.light.color). relights_holders: null until Mike answers §FI.2 call 4 (can a thrown pot light a cold sconce?).
_help.oils: §FA.3 (Mike): tar sticks and keeps burning (damage over time, a patch on the floor); light oil has a low flash point and bursts once with no lingering fire. burst is fire damage at once, burn_dps fire damage per second while stuck, in the units of residents.json fire_hp.
_help.vs_creature: §FA.3 (Mike): some oils do more to certain creatures: residents.json → creatures.<name>.oil_scale. Wired 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 60) on the skeletons: residents.json creatures.skeleton.oil_scale times every burst, stuck burn and patch.
_help.vs_boss: §FA.4, open (§FI.2 call 3). Claude's first guess: a pot never kills a boss; a hit drives it off into the dark for drives_off_s. Wired 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 60 part 2) on the snake (Boss.drive_off): a burst within splash_m of any part of its body, or a burning tar patch it lies in, sends it down below the tomb as the light does (gone the moment you can't see it) for drives_off_s, the chase off; then it comes up out of its hole or the dark nearest it.
_help.wick: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60, §FA.3): the lit wick, in your hand and in the air. flame_scale: its flame card against a campfire's; light_range_m and energy: its small amber light (§EX.6); as it catches the light flares to flare_energy and settles over flare_s (Mike: 'lighting it lights you up too'). First guesses; Mike tunes them by playing.
_help.look: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60, §FA.3): how its fire looks, all in the hearth's amber (§EX.6). flash_*: the burst per oil, its seconds, its fireball against a campfire's flame, its light's spike. patch_*: tar burning on the floor, its flames, light and reach. stuck_*: tar burning on a creature. gutter_share: the last share of a fire's life in which it dims, reddens and sinks before it goes out. char_color: the black left on the stone where it burnt. First guesses.
_help.found: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60, §FA.3 sources: found, Claude's first guess): one pot lies on the floor of a side room per dungeon, never on the spine (crawler.json plan.spine; until it's built, never on the way from the hearth room to the heart), never the hearth room or the heart, a dead end where there is one. oils: the odds of each oil. Right click takes it.
_help.dev_items: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60): F9 in the crawler (dev_mode) puts pots in the pack up to carry_max, of these oils in turn, so both can be tried.
_help.spread: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60, §FA.3 spreads_to): what catches burns burn_s seconds by its kind, burning what stands in it at burn_dps (residents.json fire_hp units), then lies charred and never burns again. In the tomb so far: the hearth room's reed mat (rushes) and the bedroll (cloth); the tomb has no dry wood. Webs and the cats' runs come with their worlds. First guesses.
_help.hurts_you: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60), open for Mike: your own pot's fire doesn't hurt you (Harm isn't in the crawler yet, prompt 56). true would make standing in a burst or a burning patch a hit. Mike, 7 Oct ("your own fire pot should be able to hurt you if you throw it way too close to yourself, like a wall or floor you're right next to"): true, wired (Claude Code; FirePots.burst_hurts_you). hurts_you_m (new, Claude Code's first guess): your own burst within this many metres of your body (your capsule, from your feet to your eye, 0.35 m round), with no stone between, is one hit (death cause fire:pot), whichever oil; looking level the shortest throw lands 4 m out (throw.min_m), so it takes a wall or floor right next to you, or looking straight down. Its burning patch and stuck tar never hurt you (first guess, open for Mike). A pot that goes off in your hand is cook_off_in_hand's one hit, never two.

throw._help_lob: Added by Claude Code (prompt 60): the pot leaves your hand lob_deg above where you look, at the speed that lands it at the charged range on level ground when you look level (looking down throws shorter, up higher and longer); it falls at gravity_mps2. arc_shown: a faint dotted arc of the lob while you aim (AimArc's look, §FB's 'keep holding to aim'). flight_max_s: longer in the air, it bursts where it is. 18 degrees keeps a full 14 m lob under a 2.6 m corridor ceiling.

tar.mike: do more damage over time and keeps them on fire

light_oil.mike: more damage in one burst, but no lingering damage over time
